title: India, Brazil move to expand trade pact beyond existing tariff lines
content:
Brazil and India are moving to expand their India-Mercosur Preferential Trade Agreement, with terms of reference completed for broader negotiations. 
The expansion could cover goods, services and investment, while electronic Certificates of Origin will facilitate paperless trade. 
Both countries aim to double bilateral trade to $30 billion by 2030.

title: India, US trade talks move towards interim pact: Goyal
content:
India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said talks with US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer focused on an early interim trade agreement. 
For exporters, apparel makers and sourcing teams, the pact could shape relative access to the US market. 
The meeting followed February's BTA framework and comes amid further negotiations after changes in US tariffs.

title: Pakistan yarn enters Bangladesh's sourcing mix: What changes by 2029?
content:
India's DGTR has issued final findings on PET film and jute products from Bangladesh, with duties recommended but not yet notified.
Pakistan's High Commissioner met BKMEA on sourcing yarn, fabrics, denim, dyes and chemicals; no commercial agreement was announced.
As Bangladesh nears LDC graduation on November 24, 2026, sourcing ties, market access and rules of origin through 2029 are in focus.

title: Indian cotton MSP up 7.2%: What changes when the duty returns?
content:
India’s 2026-27 cotton season starts on October 1 with medium-staple MSP up 7.2 per cent and long staple up 6.9 per cent.
Medium-staple MSP is ₹8,267 a quintal and long staple ₹8,667.
Cotton duty exemption runs to October 31; the normal 11 per cent import-duty burden may resume on November 1.
CCI procurement and stock sales will show whether MSP becomes binding for mills.

title: Cotton yarn dips in north India amid weakness in market
content:
Cotton yarn prices decline in Ludhiana and Delhi as weak downstream demand, payment constraints and lower cotton weigh on sentiment.
Ludhiana drops ₹5 per kg and Delhi loses ₹5-6 per kg amid limited export and domestic garment orders, fabric demand and pressure on weaving.
Panipat recycled yarn is largely stable; north Indian cotton holds steady as mills buy new-crop cotton for immediate needs.

title: India extends RoDTEP scheme till December 31, rates unchanged
content:
India has extended the RoDTEP scheme until December 31, 2026, continuing duty-remission support for eligible exports.
DGFT said it will apply to DTA units, AA holders, SEZ units and EOUs, with existing rates and value caps unchanged.
The move gives textiles, apparel, leather, engineering goods and other exporters predictability for October-December shipments.

title: Bangladesh RMG hits record $643 mn in new-market breakthrough
content:
Bangladesh’s non-traditional RMG exports reached a record $642.93 million in August 2026, or 17.82 per cent of total RMG exports.
In July-August FY2026-27, non-traditional exports rose 6.48 per cent year on year, but the EU and US share was 68.13 per cent.
TexPro shows destination concentration eased, yet the top four non-traditional HS4 apparel groups made up 61.89 per cent of the basket.

title: India extends RoSCTL scheme for apparel exports to Dec 31
content:
India has extended RoSCTL support for apparel, garments and made-ups exports for October 1-December 31, 2026. 
The scheme will continue at existing rates and under current guidelines, giving exporters and sourcing teams near-term pricing certainty. 
More than 15,400 exporters across over 444 districts benefited in 2025-26, mainly MSMEs in dispersed manufacturing clusters.

title: 10 markets still take 75% of Bangladesh apparel; can 18 change that?
content:
Bangladesh is preparing separate export strategies for 18 trading destinations, from the US, UK and France to China, India, Japan and Brazil.
RMG exports were $38.70 billion in FY2025-26, 80.62 per cent of merchandise exports, while the top 10 apparel destinations held 75.44 per cent.
TexPro shows four HS4 apparel groups made up 60.41 per cent of value, underscoring the product trap.
